children: Bank of America has a Keurig Dr Pepper

on its US 1 List of high conviction picks ahead of the company's business separation into Beverage Co. and Global Coffee Co. planned for early 2027. The firm sees a value unlock at Beverage Co. as the most compelling, with an opportunity for valuation re-rating driven by strong fundamentals.

Analyst Peter Galbo noted Beverage Co. is stronger now compared to ten years ago since Dr Pepper has surpassed the Pepsi brand by U.S. market share. "Innovation across zero sugar & flavors should drive consistent MSD topline momentum. Further, success is building, as KDP insources distribution routes from third parties to improve in-store execution/margins," he added. BofA sees valuation upside for Bev Co to 13X to 17X EV/EBITDA, or ~$31 per share.

Global Coffee Co. remains the biggest question mark, according to Galbo. Challenges seen include the need for a permanent CEO announcement, the leverage profile post-spin, and volatility in the underlying global coffee commodity given Super El Nino.

Following the planned separation, Beverage Co. is expected to own the company’s refreshment-beverage portfolio. Its major brands include Dr Pepper, Canada Dry, 7UP, A&W, Snapple, Mott’s, Bai, Core Hydration, Clamato, Peñafiel, Squirt, Sunkist, Ghost Energy, and Electrolit; it also has beverage partnerships and distribution relationships involving brands such as C4 Energy, Bloom Nutrition, and Vita Coco

Global Coffee Co. is expected to own the combined Keurig Dr Pepper and JDE Peet’s coffee businesses. Its principal brands include Keurig, Green Mountain Coffee Roasters, The Original Donut Shop, McCafé, Peet’s Coffee, Jacobs, L’OR, Douwe Egberts, Kenco, Senseo, Gevalia, Tassimo, Stumptown, Intelligentsia, and Pilão.
edged 0.4% higher in premarket trading on Monday to $31.52 vs. the 52-week range of $24.88 to $33.82.

title: BofA sees 'compelling' value in Keurig Dr Pepper after its business split
